readability.reads_as: a slow sink with the strip rolling, then a quick rise: the dip reads backwards
readability.note: The swoop down is 0.55 -> 0.41 m over 0.6-2.2 s (TCP 0.2 m/s, strip tip 1.0 m/s: mostly a strip roll), then the rise 'back up past the hub' 2.3-3.0 s is the fastest move (0.66 m/s, J2 77 %, J6 76 % accel). A bird's dip should be the fast part. Depth is floor-bound: the strip's lower end stays 0.12-0.15 m over the floor while the TCP sinks. greet_11_dive dives 0.77 m and reads.

awkward.evidence: J6 range 64 deg, strip tip 1.0 m/s vs TCP 0.2 m/s on the descent; strip lower end 0.12 m
twitches J4 1 (1.3 deg reversal) on a 0.15 m/s blip after the rise

audience.note: Seen, but from AUDIENCE SIDE it is a 0.25 m up-and-down with the strip fanning, not a swoop.

suggestions.why: a dive needs height to swoop from; at TCP 0.55 m the descent is 0.14 m and floor-bound, so the rise is the accent; greet_11_dive covers the family
